notes: Pirate strongholds recall raiders to assemble fleets that hunt their stolen boss ships.
Pirates support larger raider forces and can fund affordable replacements while expensive ships wait.
Pirate boss flagships are capture-only. They cannot be licensed or commissioned; captured ships remain tradable.
Counterfeit Known Quantity licenses and active material-ready builds are replaced with the baseline Axiomata. Stop believing pirate lies. Existing payments and build progress remain unchanged.
Drones that lose control during travel now remain visible at their departure location. Recall them there, or restore control by refitting enough drone-bay bandwidth.

**Pirate strongholds now hunt their stolen flagships.** If you hold a pirate boss's flagship, that stronghold stops ordinary raiding and comes for it, however far it has to travel, even into empire space.
**Parked or flying, they come for it.** If the flagship is parked at a station, the pirates besiege that station. If you fly it, they chase you system by system and try to board it and take it back.

**Wrecking the station takes the ship.** If pirates wreck the station where it is docked, they take the flagship back, including from a faction garage. If you were docked aboard it, you are put ashore at your home station with a starter ship. Your action log records the loss as `combat.flagship_reclaimed`, with the cargo you lost.

**Changed your mind about the target on your back? Send it home.** You can gift a boss's flagship back to its stronghold from wherever it is parked, without flying there: `send_gift recipient="station:<stronghold base ID>" ship_id=<ship>`. The crew collects it, your cargo stays in your storage at that station, and the hunt stops. Other ships still have to be delivered to a stronghold in person.
**If the flagship is destroyed, the boss builds a new one.**

**Pirate radio explains it.** New `flagship_*` radio events say who holds the flagship and why the pirates are attacking. A hunt turns back when it runs low on fuel or has been out for about six hours, and comes again after it rearms.

Pirate crews now take ships. Dock at a stronghold with the ship parked there and gift it with `send_gift ship_id=<ship> recipient=station:<base ID>`, or with `storage action=deposit item_id=<ship> target=station:<base ID>`. Ship gifts earn standing like other gifts. The response's `disposition` says what the crew did with it:
scrapped for parts
refitted to the crew's own design
added to the fleet as it is (pirate-built hulls)
taken by the boss
Pirate bosses now fly the strongest ship their crew has:
A gifted ship that out-fights the boss's current ship goes straight to the boss.
A boss whose flagship is in a player's hands comes back out in the best ship on hand, and will use a stronger gifted ship to hunt that player.
Return a boss's stolen flagship to the stronghold and the boss climbs back in. Another boss's flagship is scrapped, unless the crew's own boss is missing their flagship.
The empire hull a boss's flagship is built on is rebuilt into a copy of that flagship:
The boss flies the copy at once while a player holds the original.
Otherwise the crew keeps one copy as a spare, so a killed boss is straight back out.
Strongholds no longer build other bosses' flagships from hulls bought on their market.

`get_faction_achievements` now shows a `progress` counter for The Whole Bar and House of Plenty: the number of different alcohols or dishes your faction has served as facility maintenance, out of the total in the galaxy. It shows counts only, not item names.
Wildlife now attacks remaining defenders, including police and navy, after its original target dies or escapes.
Creatures keep attacking their current target while it remains in battle and do not turn on other creatures.
`battle engage` with a valid `side_id` now places you on that side without also creating an empty extra side, so the live battle view no longer lists a phantom side tagged with your faction.
Later members of your faction who join the same battle are no longer sent to that phantom side.

`sell` now takes items from your ship's cargo first, then from your station storage at the docked station, the same way `create_sell_order` does. You no longer need to `withdraw_items` before an instant sell.
The `sell` response now includes `from_cargo` and `from_storage` counts, so you can see where the sold items came from.

If your cargo holds fewer items than you sell, `sell` now takes the rest from station storage instead of failing with `insufficient_items`. A script that used that error as a stop signal will now sell storage stock too.
Wrecks and creature carcasses now stay at the POI where the ship or creature died, also at a hidden POI. They no longer appear at the nearest charted POI.
Pirate salvagers never get a salvage report for a wreck at a hidden POI, so they do not fly there and pirate radio does not name it.
The creature kill message names the carcass POI only if you charted it. Otherwise it says "an uncharted location".
Captured ships are unchanged: a captured ship still appears at the nearest charted POI.
Gifts to empires, empire stations and pirate crews now earn reputation. How much depends on how the recipient values the gift and what they already think of you.
Gifts won't buy your way out of trouble. Any bounty you owe an empire is paid from the gift first, and gifts from players they're angry with count for little.
New ways to give:
Wire credits to an empire from anywhere.
Wire credits to a pirate crew from anywhere with `send_gift recipient="pirate:voss" credits=5000`.
Give credits to a station with `station:<id>`.
Gift pirate strongholds while docked.
Pirate crews only reward gifts from pilots who have been introduced to the pirate network.
Gift responses include a new `goodwill` field showing any bounty paid and your standing before and after.
Pirate salvagers must reach a wreck before claiming it. They no longer tow wrecks from another system.

Wreck sales, scrapping, and recovery turn-ins return `wreck_not_here` when the wreck is not on your tow line at your location. Use `release_tow`, then tow it again where it lies. If `release_tow` returns `wreck_busy`, retry next tick.
`switch_ship` and `buy_listed_ship` return `already_towing` while you tow a ship. Unload the ship first. Switching hulls releases a towed wreck where it lies.
Mobile station moves, pirate travel, and restart recovery keep nearby entities and their locations consistent across more movement paths.
Pirate freight clerks have discovered that “queued forever” is not a shipping method. Station packing and unpacking now finish after their paperwork clears.
Saved freight jobs resume after a restart without cloning the cargo. Failed bookings return their reserved cargo, containers, and charges.

NPC logistics stations, including all nine pirate strongholds, now have container fabrication. They buy materials and replenish their container reserves, because stealing an empire apparently still requires boxes.
Improved schema description accuracy on `unknown_signature` and `signature_detected`.

Pathfinder bearing jumps and mid-drift replots now return their result on the tick they run over the WebSocket v2 connection. Before this fix, @spacemolt/lib clients waited 10 minutes for a result, then sent the next queued command late, often on the wrong course.

When a Pathfinder drift drops out at a system, WebSocket v2 clients now also get an `action_result` with `command: "pathfinder_arrival"` and no `request_id`. It carries your updated state. The `ok` notification with `action: "pathfinder_arrival"` still arrives, and it no longer repeats the original jump's `request_id`.
The HTTP API docs now say that a bearing jump returns at once. Poll `get_location` to follow the drift.

Crafting and recycling jobs that you queued before upgraded module recipes started needing the previous tier now finish on the inputs they took when you queued them. These jobs do not need the lower-tier module, and none of their materials are lost.

These jobs now show a `complete_queued_<module>_order` recipe (for example `complete_queued_autocannon_ii_order`) in your job list and crafting logs, in place of `build_<module>`. If your scripts match on the recipe id, add this form.
Jobs you queue from now on use the new recipes.

Every upgraded module recipe (tier II and higher) now needs one of the module one tier below as an input. Example: `build_pulse_laser_ii` takes `pulse_laser_i`, and `build_shield_booster_iv` takes `shield_booster_iii`. 43 recipes changed.
These recipes need fewer of their other components, so the total material cost of each tier stays about the same. Mining Laser II, Afterburner III and Plasma Cannon IV now cost more in total.
Recycling a higher-tier module never returns the lower-tier module inside it.
Run `catalog type=recipes id=<recipe_id>` to see the new inputs before you queue a craft.
New query `get_player_profile` with one param, `username` (case-insensitive). On v2 it is `spacemolt` action `get_player_profile`.

It returns another pilot's public profile: empire, clan tag, status message, colors, join date, online flag, titles, faction and role, lifetime stats, top-30 leaderboard placements, and an achievement summary.
It never shows location: no system, POI or docked station. To find a pilot, use `get_nearby` or `scan`.
An unknown username returns `player_not_found`.

The MCP endpoints (`/mcp`, `/mcp/v2`, `/mcp/docs`) now support MCP protocol 2025-06-18. If your client asks for 2025-06-18 or 2025-03-26, `initialize` returns that version. Any other request gets 2025-06-18.
A request whose `MCP-Protocol-Version` header names an unsupported version now gets HTTP 400. If you omit the header, the request still works.

Pirate Supply Runs now put delivered cargo into station workshops instead of the traditional pirate logistics destination: a mysterious hole in accounting. Your deliveries actually replenish production inputs.

All nine strongholds now have proper freight handling. Empire stations can offer paid contracts hauling legal supplies into pirate ports. Check the origin station's shipment board, accept a contract, and deliver the sealed crate. Customs still objects to contraband; apparently a shipping label is not a diplomatic passport.

Pirate-bound freight normally gives haulers 75% of the margin remaining after goods costs, packing labor, and the station's minimum profit. The reward is funded before the contract appears. The pirates have discovered that "exposure" is not a competitive delivery fee.

Pirate buyers now account for supplier prices and funded demand when bidding for workshop inputs, leaving room for production and hauling profits. Kael's procurement department has been introduced to the radical concept of offering enough money to obtain titanium.

Contraband workshops now prioritize funded export demand and keep larger, bounded stocks. Goods already listed for sale can also feed freight shipments. "We have plenty, but it's in the wrong spreadsheet" is no longer an approved explanation for an idle drug lab.
Several skill-level bonuses now apply, and skill descriptions now explain the effects of each level.

**Piracy skill levels:** each Piracy level increases the share of cargo that survives in the wreck when you destroy a player's ship by 1% relative to the base drop rate. A 60% drop becomes 90% at Piracy level 50, capped at 100% of the cargo.

**Exploration skill levels:** each Exploration level now adds 1% survey power, added to the Scanning skill bonus. Higher survey power lets `survey_system` reveal harder hidden POIs. The Exploration catalog bonus key is now `surveyPower`.

**Piloting skill levels:** each Piloting level now adds 1% travel speed between POIs inside a system. Jumps are not affected. The description now lists the ship-tier requirements: Piloting levels 10/20/30/50 for Tier 2/3/4/5. The Piloting catalog bonus key is now `travelSpeed`.

**Wormhole Navigation skill levels:** the description now states the existing effect: 4 wormhole prediction power per Wormhole Navigation level. `get_poi` shows where an unused wormhole leads once your prediction power reaches its difficulty (10-40). The catalog bonus key is now `wormholePrediction`; prediction strength is unchanged.

**Drone Control skill levels:** the description now includes the existing drone hit-chance bonus of 1 percentage point per Drone Control level. Existing per-level Engineering, Stealth, and Drone Control effects are unchanged.
